## Phase 1: Context Gathering

## Phase 2: Initial Proposal

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FEATURE SPEC PROPOSAL: Version Endpoint
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: Version Endpoint
  As an operator or monitoring system
  I want to retrieve version metadata from the api_test service
  So that I can identify the running build and service version

  Background:
    Given the api_test service is running
    And the version endpoint is available

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (3 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core path — GET returns version metadata for a healthy service
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Retrieving version information succeeds
    When I request GET /version
    Then the response status should be 200
    And the response should contain the application version
    And the response should contain the git commit hash
    And the response should contain the service name

  # Why: Demonstrates no-auth access — endpoint is publicly accessible
  @key-example
  Scenario: Version information is accessible without authentication
    Given I am not authenticated
    When I request GET /version
    Then the request should succeed
    And all version fields should be present

  # Why: Demonstrates no-database dependency — response is self-contained
  @key-example
  Scenario: Version information is available without database access
    Given the database is unavailable
    When I request GET /version
    Then the request should succeed
    And all version fields should be present

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (3 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — empty version values are not returned
  @boundary
  Scenario: Version fields are guaranteed to be populated
    When I request GET /version
    Then every version field should contain a non-empty value

  # Why: Just-outside boundary — response shape is exact
  @boundary
  Scenario: Version response contains exactly three fields
    When I request GET /version
    Then the response should contain exactly three fields
    And no additional fields should be present

  # Why: Just-inside boundary for available format — no doc-string wrapper
  @boundary
  Scenario: Version response uses the configured service name
    When I request GET /version
    Then the service name field should match the configured service name

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (4 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Enforces read-only constraint — all write methods rejected
  @negative
  Scenario Outline: Write methods on the version endpoint are rejected
    When I send <method> /version
    Then the response status should be 405
    And the operation should be rejected

    Examples:
      | method |
      | POST   |
      | PUT    |
      | PATCH  |
      | DELETE |

  # Why: Method not allowed is consistent — no alternative method accepted
  @negative
  Scenario: A write method on the version endpoint does not modify data
    Given I have retrieved the current version information
    When I send POST /version
    Then the response status should be 405
    And the version information should remain unchanged

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Failure isolation — version endpoint works when dependent systems fail
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Version endpoint returns data when the database is down
    Given the database is down
    When I request GET /version
    Then the request should succeed
    And all version fields should be present

  # Why: Consistency across metadata endpoints — same access pattern
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Version endpoint follows the same pattern as uptime and stats endpoints
    Given the uptime endpoint is accessible
    When I request GET /version
    Then the response format should match the uptime endpoint pattern

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Total: 12 scenarios across 4 groups
Inferred assumptions: 5 (will be resolved in Phase 5)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

---

## Phase 3: Human Curation

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CURATION: Review each group
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each group, you may:

  [A] Accept  — include all scenarios in this group as-is
  [R] Reject  — exclude all scenarios in this group
  [M] Modify  — accept but specify changes (provide inline)
  [+] Add     — accept and add additional scenarios you describe
  [?] Defer   — mark group for future specification; excluded from output

Fast path: type "A A A A" to accept all four groups at once.

GROUP A — Key Examples (3 scenarios): _
GROUP B — Boundary Conditions (3 scenarios): _
GROUP C — Negative Cases (4 scenarios): _
GROUP D — Edge Cases (2 scenarios): _
```

Please provide your curation decisions for each group.

---

## Phase 4: Edge Case Expansion (optional)

I've identified additional scenarios covering security, concurrency, and integration boundaries:

**Security (2):**
- Version endpoint does not leak internal build paths or secrets in response
- Version endpoint rejects malformed HTTP methods (e.g., CONNECT) with 405

**Concurrency (1):**
- Concurrent requests to version endpoint all succeed with identical data

**Integration boundaries (2):**
- Version endpoint responds correctly when the underlying application metadata file is missing
- Version endpoint responds when the git commit hash is not injected (looking for degraded mode)

Include them? [Y/S/N]:
